Russian lines and forts (Irtysh, Ishim, Orenburg, Siberian line) behind the confidence-1 losses of 1718, 1721, 1738 and 1769 are undated on every page opened; open Orenburg, Semipalatinsk, Omsk, Siberian Line, Russian conquest of Central Asia

The 1791 Khiva loss (725 cells), the 1809 Kokand loss of the Sayram-Turkestan lands (259 cells) and the 1822 Kokand loss (396 cells) are Cliopatria's; only the 1809 Tashkent annexation and 'the 1820s' are on a page; open Khanate of Khiva and the Syr Darya line of Kokand

The date of the Uzbek handover of the Syr Darya lands to Kasym (1510, confidence 1) and of the Dzungars' 1745 withdrawal from Tashkent are bridging judgments; the Kasym Khan, Shaybanids, Abu'l-Khayr Khan and Kerei Khan pages were thin
Lesser Jüz page did not load, so the Junior jüz's lands (Ural, Emba, Aral, Mangyshlak), the 1731 oath and the Bukey Horde rest on the Kazakh Khanate and Jüz pages only

Russian suzerainty over the Junior (1731) and Middle (1740) jüzes, the Dzungar overlordship of the jüzes (1734-1742) and the Qing suzerainty over Abylai (1757) are not in this ledger, because vassal events belong to the overlord's dossier; they need vassal_start/vassal_end with counterpart kazakh-khanate in russian-empire, dzungar-khanate and qing-dynasty

problems: Cliopatria's Kazakh Khanate shapes of 1475-1501 take 1,925 cells (Samarkand, Bukhara, Kashkadarya, Surkhandarya, Khatlon, Tashkent) from its Timurid shape; no opened page supports this and two contradict it (Moghulistan page: Tashkent from the Timurids in 1482 or 1484; Muhammad Shaybani page: Samarkand from the Timurids in 1500). Verdict adjust (Uzbekistan, Tajikistan and Turkmenistan removed); the timurid-empire and shaybanids dossiers should be checked for double claims.

Mirror events do not coincide by year: khanate-of-sibir dates the steppe loss to the Kazakhs 1468 and 1487 (this dossier: gain 1470, 1487); nogai-horde ends its 1568 contest and loses the steppe in 1572 (this dossier: contest end and gain 1569, from the Kazakh Khanate page); nogai-horde 1520-1521 matches.

The page budget (14) is spent on 14 opened pages, of which Kasym Khan, Shaybanids, Abu'l-Khayr Khan and Kerei Khan turned out thin; seventeen ledger events are at confidence 1 (Cliopatria's shapes or bridging judgments, page silent).

Cliopatria draws the Kazakh Khanate as one state to 1847; the pages have the three jüzes effectively independent from about 1715-1721, the Middle and Junior khanates abolished by Russia in 1817-1824 and a last khan, Kenesary, only in 1841-1847. The dossier follows Cliopatria and hatches the steppe as Russian 1822-1837 (Middle jüz) and 1824-1847 (Junior jüz) with a contest zone 1837-1847.
